# What this file does

The Policymaker version of the country health financing profile examines fourteen questions that ministries of finance and health discuss together: how large the health budget is and what accounted for its change over ten years, how the country's health spending relates to health and financial protection, whether funding reaches health workers, medicines and services, how funds are pooled and providers paid, how much more economic growth and a higher health share of the budget could provide by 2031, and what additional funding might buy. The deck answers these questions in 22 slides: a cover, a contents page, fourteen main slides, an annex on the main performance gap, and six annex slides repeating the money slides at market exchange rates in US$.

We rebuild every number the slides print and draw the main figure of each slide. We set the country with the header's `iso` code. Changing it, or calling `rmarkdown::render("country-financing-brief.Rmd", params = list(iso = "ETH"))`, rebuilds the document for another country. The last section checks the numbers against the deck's text for the fifteen countries whose deck text is stored with the data.

**Data.** Everything the file reads is in `data/` as RDS files, read with relative paths, and `data/README.md` describes each one. The sources are the WHO Global Health Expenditure Database (2025 update), WHO health accounts by function, the World Bank's World Development Indicators and income groups, WHO and World Bank UHC monitoring (service coverage and financial hardship), WHO national health workforce accounts, the IMF World Economic Outlook (October 2026) and its government finance statistics, the UN World Population Prospects 2024, and provider payment records. Nothing is downloaded while the file runs.

**How to run it.** Open the folder in RStudio (or make it the working directory) and knit `country-financing-brief.Rmd`. From a terminal: `Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("country-financing-brief.Rmd", params = list(iso = "KEN"))'`. A run takes under a minute.

**Packages.** rmarkdown, knitr, dplyr, tidyr, tibble, scales, ggplot2, ggrepel, systemfonts and ragg (R 4.1 or later). The figures use Open Sans, bundled in `fonts/` under the SIL Open Font Licence, so no font has to be installed.

**Conventions on every slide.**

* The year. Every "latest" value is taken at or before 2023, the deck's default year.
* Comparators. The country's World Bank income group, the country included. A median is published only when at least 8 members report and they are at least 70% of the group, the rule the website applies to every statistic.
* Money. The country's own amounts are in its currency at constant 2023 prices: GHED's US$ figure times GHED's 2023 exchange rate (GDP in national currency over GDP in US$). Levels compared across countries are in PPP international dollars. The annex repeats the money slides in US$.
* Rounding. JavaScript, which draws the deck, rounds a half away from zero on the shortest decimal form of a number. R's `formatC()` rounds the stored binary value instead, so `num()` nudges such a number up by two units in its last place before rounding, and a printed "0.13" here is a printed "0.13" on the slide.

# Setup

```{r setup, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# We shape the data with dplyr and tidyr, draw with ggplot2 and ggrepel, and use systemfonts
# with ragg so that the figures can use Open Sans without installing it
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
library(systemfonts)
library(ragg)

# We register Open Sans from fonts/ by relative path. A computer that already has Open Sans
# keeps its own copy, because systemfonts refuses to register a name the system already has.
known_fonts <- c(system_fonts()$family, registry_fonts()$family)
if (!"Open Sans" %in% known_fonts) {
  register_font(
    "Open Sans",
    plain = "fonts/OpenSans-Regular.ttf",
    bold = "fonts/OpenSans-Bold.ttf",
    italic = "fonts/OpenSans-Italic.ttf",
    bolditalic = "fonts/OpenSans-BoldItalic.ttf"
  )
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  dev = "ragg_png",
  dpi = 150,
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 5.2,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "", dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)
# we want every text layer in Open Sans unless a layer says otherwise
update_geom_defaults("text", list(family = "Open Sans"))

# the World Bank colours of the deck
WB <- c(
  teal = "#0071bc",
  dark = "#002244",
  rust = "#b5452c",
  grey = "#9aa3ad",
  muted = "#5b6470",
  light = "#e3e7ea",
  faint = "#c9d0d6",
  gold = "#b07d12",
  ink = "#13212f",
  tint = "#e8f2fa",
  mid = "#86b5df",
  pale = "#cfe2f3"
)

# One theme for every figure. ggplot2 has no ready theme with black x and y axis lines, so we
# build ours once: Open Sans, black axis lines and ticks, light horizontal gridlines, the
# legend on top.
theme_deck <- function(base_size = 12) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size, base_family = "Open Sans") +
    theme(
      axis.line = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5),
      axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4),
      axis.text = element_text(colour = WB[["ink"]]),
      axis.title = element_text(colour = WB[["ink"]], face = "bold", size = rel(0.9)),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = WB[["light"]], linewidth = 0.35),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", colour = WB[["dark"]], size = rel(1.05)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = WB[["muted"]]),
      plot.caption = element_text(colour = WB[["muted"]], hjust = 0, size = rel(0.75)),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", colour = WB[["ink"]], hjust = 0),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.caption.position = "plot"
    )
}
```

# Data

We keep the financing panel as a long table, with one row per country, indicator and year with a published value; missing years are absent, never zero. The outcome series follows the same structure. For lookups and joins we use a wide copy, one row per country and year, so the file stays quick when a slide fits a line across every country in several years.

```{r data}
# We read every input from data/ by relative path
countries <- readRDS("data/countries.rds") # 195 countries, in the deck's own order
group_labels <- readRDS("data/group_labels.rds") # income-group and region labels
fin <- readRDS("data/ghed_financing.rds") # WHO GHED financing series, long
gstats <- readRDS("data/ghed_group_stats.rds") # the site's group medians and quartiles
outc <- readRDS("data/outcomes.rds") # outcomes and coverage (WDI, WHO GHO, UHC monitoring)
lcu_cur <- readRDS("data/lcu_currency.rds") # currency, GHED's 2023 rate, or why there is none
lcu_ser <- readRDS("data/lcu_series.rds") # exchange rate, PPP factor and deflators by year
imf_fiscal <- readRDS("data/imf_fiscal.rds") # IMF net lending and revenue, % of GDP
imf_weo <- readRDS("data/imf_weo_projections.rds") # IMF WEO October 2026 paths to 2031
wpp <- readRDS("data/wpp_funding.rds") # UN WPP 2024 population, deaths, value per death
prevention <- readRDS("data/ghed_prevention.rds") # GHED preventive and curative care shares
medicines <- readRDS("data/ghed_medicines.rds") # GHED HC.5.1 medicines share and its payers
med_avail <- readRDS("data/medicine_availability.rds") # SDG 3.b.3 medicine availability
workforce <- readRDS("data/workforce.rds") # doctors, nurses and midwives, beds per 1,000
cofog <- readRDS("data/imf_cofog_health.rds") # IMF government health spending by function
pay_rec <- readRDS("data/payment_records.rds") # what each provider payment record holds
pay_arr <- readRDS("data/payment_arrangements.rds") # provider payment arrangements
pay_methods <- readRDS("data/payment_methods.rds") # payment method names
credits <- readRDS("data/cover_credits.rds") # cover photograph credits
flags <- readRDS("data/country_flags.rds") # GHED years with a negative private residual

# We spread the financing panel to one row per country and year with one column per
# indicator, because most steps below read several indicators of the same year
fin_wide <- pivot_wider(fin, names_from = code, values_from = value)
```

# Shared computations

We use shared calculations across the slides: the spending identity in one year, its change over ten years, two cross-country fits, medians, and the fiscal projection. We make each calculation once, in the deck's order, and explain each rule.

## Statistics and number formats

We calculate medians and quartiles as the deck does: the plain median and the quartile that interpolates between ranks (R's type 7). We fit lines with `lm()`. We print numbers with `formatC()`, which groups thousands with commas. JavaScript, which draws the deck, rounds the shortest decimal form of a number half away from zero (2.675 to 2.68). To match that rule, `num()` first moves such a number up by two units in its last place before rounding.

```{r helpers-numbers}
# The income-group median as the website publishes it. median() does the arithmetic; we add
# the website's reporting rule, which no standard function knows: no median from fewer than 8
# reporting countries, or from less than 70% of the group's members.
peer_median <- function(values) {
  reported <- values[is.finite(values)]
  too_few <- length(reported) < 8 || length(reported) / length(INC_MEMBERS) < 0.7
  if (too_few) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }
  median(reported)
}

NA_TXT <- "Not available" # what the deck prints for a missing value
NB <- " " # the deck puts a no-break space after a currency code

# Numbers as the deck prints them: rounded with formatC(), commas for thousands, an optional
# prefix ("US$") or suffix ("%"), and "Not available" when the value is missing. With
# plus = TRUE a change carries its sign, except a change that rounds to zero.
num <- function(x, digits = 1, prefix = "", suffix = "", plus = FALSE) {
  # JavaScript, which draws the deck, rounds the shortest decimal form of a number half away
  # from zero (2.675 to 2.68, 0.125 to 0.13). formatC() rounds the stored binary value, which
  # for 2.675 lies just below the half, and sends an exact half to the even digit. So we move a
  # number with a short decimal form up by two units in the last place before rounding.
  finite <- is.finite(x)
  is_short <- finite
  is_short[finite] <- as.numeric(sprintf("%.15g", x[finite])) == x[finite]
  nudged <- ifelse(is_short, x * (1 + 2 * .Machine$double.eps), x)
  text <- formatC(nudged, format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ",")
  if (plus) {
    sign_text <- case_when(abs(x) < 0.5 / 10^digits ~ "", x > 0 ~ "+", TRUE ~ "-")
    text <- paste0(sign_text, formatC(abs(nudged), format = "f", digits = digits, big.mark = ","))
  }
  ifelse(is.finite(x), paste0(prefix, text, suffix), NA_TXT)
}

# We keep the printed values of each slide for the check at the end
slide_values <- list()
```

## The country, its comparators and its currency

We use the country's short form in running text: the name without a bracketed part, or the ISO code when that name is still longer than 24 characters. We compare the country with members of its income group, including the country itself, and use the members of its World Bank region to choose the four countries named on the scatter charts.

We convert to local currency with exact identities on GHED's own figures. A 2023 amount in US$ times GHED's 2023 rate gives the amount in national currency at 2023 prices. We convert another year's current US$ amount at that year's rate and deflate it with GHED's GDP price index. We use no rate that GHED does not publish. A country without a 2023 rate (Cuba) shows US$ on every slide, as the deck does.

```{r context}
MAX_YEAR <- 2023 # the deck's default year: every latest value is at or before it
BASE <- 2023 # constant prices and the PPP base year
ISO <- toupper(params$iso)
if (!ISO %in% countries$iso3) {
  stop("No country with the code ", ISO, " in data/countries.rds")
}
ISOS <- countries$iso3 # every country, in the deck's order
CTRY <- filter(countries, iso3 == ISO)
NAME <- CTRY$name

# In running text the deck uses the name without a bracketed part, or the ISO code when that
# is still longer than 24 characters
SHORT <- trimws(sub("\\s*\\(.*\\)\\s*$", "", NAME))
if (nchar(SHORT) > 24) {
  SHORT <- ISO
}

# the income group and its wording ("a lower-middle-income median")
INC <- CTRY$income_group
income_label <- filter(group_labels, grouping == "income", key == INC)
INC_LABEL <- income_label$label
ADJ <- income_label$adjective # e.g. "lower-middle-income"
ADJ_CAP <- paste0(toupper(substr(ADJ, 1, 1)), substring(ADJ, 2)) # "Lower-middle-income"
AN_ADJ <- ifelse(grepl("^[aeiou]", ADJ, ignore.case = TRUE), "an", "a")
INC_MEMBERS <- countries$iso3[countries$income_group == INC] # the country included
REG <- CTRY$wb_region
REG_MEMBERS <- countries$iso3[countries$wb_region == REG]

# the country's own financing rows, which we look up by year
own_fin <- filter(fin_wide, iso3 == ISO)

# The site's precomputed statistics for the income group. We keep a median only where the
# reporting rule lets the website publish it, so a withheld median reads as NA; one row per
# year and one column per indicator, looked up by year with match().
inc_stats <- filter(gstats, grouping == "income", key == INC)
inc_medians <- inc_stats |>
  mutate(median = ifelse(suppressed, NA, median)) |>
  select(year, code, median) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = code, values_from = median)

# Names on the charts: a common short form, else the name without its bracket, and the ISO
# code when that is still longer than 16 characters
ALIAS <- c(
  TZA = "Tanzania", COD = "DR Congo", PRK = "DPR Korea", LAO = "Lao PDR",
  GBR = "United Kingdom", USA = "United States", RUS = "Russia", IRN = "Iran",
  VEN = "Venezuela", BOL = "Bolivia", SYR = "Syria", KOR = "Korea, Rep.", MDA = "Moldova",
  FSM = "Micronesia", NLD = "Netherlands", TUR = "Türkiye", CZE = "Czechia"
)
countries <- countries |>
  mutate(
    label = coalesce(unname(ALIAS[iso3]), trimws(sub("\\s*\\(.*\\)\\s*$", "", name))),
    label = ifelse(nchar(label) <= 16, label, iso3)
  )

# Local currency at constant 2023 prices. Without a 2023 rate the main slides stay in US$
# and the six annex copies are left out.
LCU <- filter(lcu_cur, iso3 == ISO)
HAS_LCU <- isTRUE(is.finite(LCU$rate))
LCU_MAIN <- HAS_LCU
FALLBACK_NOTE <- NULL
if (!HAS_LCU) {
  FALLBACK_NOTE <- paste0(
    "Amounts are in US$: local-currency figures are not available for ", SHORT,
    " (", LCU$missing_reason, ")."
  )
}
CODE <- if (HAS_LCU) LCU$code else "US$"
CUR_NAME <- if (HAS_LCU) LCU$name else "US dollars"
RATE_TEXT <- NA_TXT
if (HAS_LCU) {
  # the deck prints the rate to two decimals below 100, one below 1,000 and none above
  rate_digits <- case_when(LCU$rate < 100 ~ 2, LCU$rate < 1000 ~ 1, TRUE ~ 0)
  RATE_TEXT <- paste0(CODE, NB, num(LCU$rate, rate_digits), " per US$")
}

# The factor that turns US$ of a given year into local currency at 2023 prices: GHED's 2023
# rate for 2023 itself, and for another year that year's rate deflated with GHED's GDP price
# index (2023 = 100). We look it up by year with match(); a missing year gives NA.
to_lcu <- lcu_ser |>
  filter(iso3 == ISO, year != BASE) |>
  transmute(year, factor = xr * 100 / gdpd) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(year = BASE, factor = LCU$rate))

# Money as the deck prints it. No standard function writes amounts the deck's way, so we keep
# the rule here once. In local currency a million or more is written in words with three
# significant figures; a smaller amount prints to one decimal under 10, to the unit under
# 1,000 and to the ten above (to the unit when exact = TRUE). In US$ the deck prints one
# decimal under US$10, in international (PPP) dollars one decimal under Int$50, and whole
# dollars above.
fmt_money <- function(amount, currency = "local", exact = FALSE) {
  size <- abs(amount)
  if (!is.finite(amount)) {
    return(NA_TXT)
  }
  if (currency == "US$") {
    return(num(amount, ifelse(size < 10, 1, 0), prefix = "US$"))
  }
  if (currency == "Int$") {
    return(num(amount, ifelse(size < 50, 1, 0), prefix = "Int$"))
  }
  if (size >= 1e6) {
    divisor <- case_when(size >= 1e12 ~ 1e12, size >= 1e9 ~ 1e9, TRUE ~ 1e6)
    word <- case_when(size >= 1e12 ~ "trillion", size >= 1e9 ~ "billion", TRUE ~ "million")
    in_words <- amount / divisor
    digits <- case_when(abs(in_words) >= 100 ~ 0, abs(in_words) >= 10 ~ 1, TRUE ~ 2)
    text <- paste0(num(in_words, digits), NB, word)
  } else if (exact || (size >= 10 && size < 1000)) {
    text <- num(amount, 0)
  } else if (size < 10) {
    text <- num(amount, 1)
  } else {
    text <- num(round(amount, -1), 0) # to the ten
  }
  paste0(CODE, NB, text)
}

# The deck picks the longest wording of a lead that still fits on two lines, judging width
# from a table of Open Sans letter widths (em per character). No standard function measures
# text this way, so we keep the deck's estimate as one short function. Bold letters are 8%
# wider; bold figures keep the regular width, except on the US$ copy of slide 15.
LETTER_EM <- c(
  " " = 0.26, " " = 0.26, "." = 0.263, "," = 0.259, ";" = 0.263, ":" = 0.263,
  "'" = 0.219, "(" = 0.295, ")" = 0.295, "-" = 0.322, "%" = 0.827, "+" = 0.572,
  f = 0.336, i = 0.252, j = 0.252, l = 0.252, r = 0.409, t = 0.356, c = 0.479, k = 0.525,
  s = 0.477, v = 0.5, x = 0.523, y = 0.501, z = 0.469, m = 0.926, w = 0.775, I = 0.279
)
lead_width <- function(html, bold_figures_wider = FALSE) {
  pieces <- strsplit(html, "</?b>")[[1]] # every second piece is bold
  width <- 0
  for (i in seq_along(pieces)) {
    characters <- strsplit(pieces[i], "")[[1]]
    em <- unname(LETTER_EM[characters])
    em[is.na(em) & grepl("[A-Z]", characters)] <- 0.65 # other capitals
    em[is.na(em)] <- 0.595 # every other character
    if (i %% 2 == 0) {
      keeps_width <- grepl("[0-9.,  ]", characters) & !bold_figures_wider
      em <- em * ifelse(keeps_width, 1, 1.08)
    }
    width <- width + sum(em) * 27 # the lead is set at 27 px
  }
  width
}
LEAD_LIMIT <- 2 * 1380 * 0.92 # two lines of 1,380 px, less the deck's 8% margin

# The possessive of a name ("Kenya's", "the Philippines'"); the text around the chunks calls it
poss <- function(name) ifelse(grepl("s$", name), paste0(name, "'"), paste0(name, "'s"))
```

## The spending identity in one year

GHED's figures satisfy an exact spending identity: government health spending per person equals GDP per person times government spending as a share of GDP times health's share of government spending. The comparison uses the latest year at or before 2023 when the country has all three factors and the income group has a publishable median for each; otherwise, we use the country's latest complete year without a comparison.

We can split government spending into revenue and fiscal stance (spending per unit of revenue), because spending equals revenue plus net borrowing. We calculate revenue as GHED government spending plus IMF net lending. We omit the split when IMF revenue differs from that sum by more than 5 points of GDP (8 of 148 countries in 2023), avoiding conflicting slide figures.

```{r identity}
SHORT_RATIO <- 0.95 # a step more than 5% below its median is a shortfall
FACTORS <- c("gdp_pc_usd", "gge_gdp", "gghed_gge")

# the country's years with all three factors, latest first
own_years <- own_fin |>
  filter(year <= MAX_YEAR) |>
  filter(is.finite(gdp_pc_usd), is.finite(gge_gdp), is.finite(gghed_gge)) |>
  arrange(desc(year)) |>
  pull(year)

# the years in which all three income-group medians are publishable
peer_years <- inc_stats |>
  filter(code %in% FACTORS, !suppressed, is.finite(median)) |>
  count(year) |>
  filter(n == 3) |>
  pull(year)

# We take the latest year with both. Failing that, we take the country's latest complete year,
# without a comparison.
ID <- list(year = intersect(own_years, peer_years)[1], ghe_pc = NA_real_)
ID$peer_ok <- !is.na(ID$year)
if (!ID$peer_ok) {
  ID$year <- own_years[1]
}
ID$ready <- !is.na(ID$year)

if (ID$ready) {
  identity_row <- filter(own_fin, year == ID$year)
  ID$gdp_pc <- identity_row$gdp_pc_usd
  ID$gge_gdp <- identity_row$gge_gdp
  ID$gghed_gge <- identity_row$gghed_gge
  # government health spending per person, US$
  ID$ghe_pc <- ID$gdp_pc * (ID$gge_gdp / 100) * (ID$gghed_gge / 100)

  # For every member we split government spending into revenue (GHED spending plus IMF net
  # lending) and the fiscal stance (spending per unit of revenue). We leave a member out when
  # the IMF's own revenue differs from that sum by more than 5 points of GDP.
  imf_same_year <- filter(imf_fiscal, year == ID$year)
  fiscal <- fin_wide |>
    filter(year == ID$year, iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS) |>
    select(iso3, gge_gdp) |>
    inner_join(imf_same_year, by = "iso3") |>
    mutate(rev = gge_gdp + net_lending, ratio = gge_gdp / rev) |>
    filter(is.finite(rev), rev > 0) |>
    filter(!(is.finite(revenue) & abs(rev - revenue) > 5))
  # the split is left out when the country itself fails the test
  ID$split <- ISO %in% fiscal$iso3
}
```

## The binding fiscal constraint

We value each budget step by setting it to the same-year income-group median while holding the other steps at the country's values. We count a fiscal step (revenue or fiscal stance, or government spending where revenue cannot be split) more than 5% below its median as a constraint; the primary constraint is the one with the greatest value. We compare health's share with its median but do not rank it here, because a below-peer share alone does not show that health could take more of the budget; we assess that question separately. These are distances on an identity, not forecasts.

```{r constraint}
Q09 <- list(ready = ID$ready && is.finite(ID$ghe_pc), year = ID$year, peer_ok = ID$peer_ok)
if (Q09$ready) {
  identity_year <- ID$year
  ghe_per_person <- ID$ghe_pc

  # the income-group medians of the three factors and of the result in that year (none when
  # the year has no comparison)
  median_row <- match(identity_year, inc_medians$year)
  med_gdp <- NA_real_
  med_spend <- NA_real_
  med_share <- NA_real_
  Q09$peer_med <- NA_real_
  if (ID$peer_ok) {
    med_gdp <- inc_medians$gdp_pc_usd[median_row]
    med_spend <- inc_medians$gge_gdp[median_row]
    med_share <- inc_medians$gghed_gge[median_row]
    Q09$peer_med <- inc_medians$gghed_pc_usd[median_row]
  }
  group_size <- filter(inc_stats, code == "gge_gdp", year == identity_year)$n_members
  Q09$N <- if (ID$peer_ok) group_size else length(INC_MEMBERS)

  # The steps: GDP per person, then revenue and the fiscal stance (or government spending when
  # revenue cannot be split), then health's share, each against its median
  if (ID$split) {
    own_fiscal <- filter(fiscal, iso3 == ISO)
    steps <- data.frame(
      step = c("base", "rev", "stance", "priority"),
      value = c(ID$gdp_pc, own_fiscal$rev, own_fiscal$ratio, ID$gghed_gge),
      median = c(med_gdp, peer_median(fiscal$rev), peer_median(fiscal$ratio), med_share)
    )
  } else {
    steps <- data.frame(
      step = c("base", "spend", "priority"),
      value = c(ID$gdp_pc, ID$gge_gdp, ID$gghed_gge),
      median = c(med_gdp, med_spend, med_share)
    )
  }
  # Setting one step to its median and holding the others gives the spending that step is
  # worth; a step more than 5% below its median is a shortfall
  steps <- steps |>
    mutate(
      ratio = ifelse(is.finite(value) & is.finite(median) & median != 0, value / median, NA),
      cf = ghe_per_person / ratio,
      gain = cf - ghe_per_person,
      below = is.finite(ratio) & ratio < SHORT_RATIO
    )
  Q09$ghe <- ghe_per_person
  Q09$split <- ID$split
  Q09$steps <- steps

  if (ID$peer_ok) {
    # the primary constraint: the fiscal step below its median that is worth the most
    fiscal_below <- steps |>
      filter(!step %in% c("base", "priority"), below) |>
      arrange(desc(gain))
    Q09$binding <- if (nrow(fiscal_below) > 0) fiscal_below$step[1] else NA_character_
    # health's share against its median, in words
    priority_ratio <- steps$ratio[steps$step == "priority"]
    Q09$prio_rel <- case_when(
      !is.finite(priority_ratio) ~ NA_character_,
      priority_ratio >= 1.05 ~ "above",
      priority_ratio >= 1 ~ "slightly above",
      priority_ratio >= 0.95 ~ "slightly below",
      TRUE ~ "below"
    )

    # We compare GDP per person and the result with the median in PPP. GDP per person in
    # current international $ is GHED's health spending in PPP times 100 over health spending
    # as a % of GDP.
    members_ppp <- fin_wide |>
      filter(year == identity_year, iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS) |>
      mutate(gdp_ppp = ifelse(che_gdp > 0, che_ppp_pc * 100 / che_gdp, NA))
    own_ppp <- filter(members_ppp, iso3 == ISO)
    gdp_ppp_median <- peer_median(members_ppp$gdp_ppp)
    ghe_ppp_median <- inc_medians$gghed_ppp_pc[median_row]
    gdp_ok <- is.finite(own_ppp$gdp_ppp) && is.finite(gdp_ppp_median) && gdp_ppp_median > 0
    ghe_ok <- is.finite(own_ppp$gghed_ppp_pc) && is.finite(ghe_ppp_median) && ghe_ppp_median > 0
    Q09$gdp_ppp_ratio <- if (gdp_ok) own_ppp$gdp_ppp / gdp_ppp_median else NA_real_
    Q09$ghe_ppp_ratio <- if (ghe_ok) own_ppp$gghed_ppp_pc / ghe_ppp_median else NA_real_
  }
}
```

## Ten years of change

We decompose the change in real government health spending per person into three parts that sum exactly under the identity above: GDP per person, government spending as a share of GDP, and health's share of government spending. Each part is an average annual change in log points (times 100). We end the window in the latest year at or before 2023 with all parts and start ten years earlier, or later if needed, but never less than five years before the end. For real terms we use GHED's own conversion for each country and year, constant 2023 US$ over current US$, so growth rates match local currency.

We use the same window for the direction slide's outcome rows. For each measure, we take the gap to the income-group median at the start and end (as a ratio for mortality, a difference for coverage), then call it narrowing, widening or steady under the deck's thresholds: 5% for a mortality ratio, 2 points of the coverage index, 1 point of financial hardship.

```{r trends}
WINDOW <- 10 # the window: ten years
MIN_SPAN <- 5 # or at least five when the data are shorter

# The identity's parts in real terms, every country and year. We convert GDP per person with
# GHED's own factor (constant 2023 US$ over current US$ health spending) so that growth rates
# match local currency.
parts <- fin_wide |>
  mutate(
    k = ifelse(che_usd2023_pc > 0 & che_pc_usd > 0, che_usd2023_pc / che_pc_usd, NA),
    gdp = gdp_pc_usd * k,
    pie = gge_gdp,
    slice = gghed_gge,
    ghe = gdp * (pie / 100) * (slice / 100)
  ) |>
  filter(is.finite(gdp), gdp_pc_usd > 0, pie > 0, slice > 0) |>
  select(iso3, year, gdp, pie, slice, ghe)
own_parts <- filter(parts, iso3 == ISO)
che_years <- own_fin |>
  filter(che_usd2023_pc > 0) |>
  pull(year)

# The window: the latest end year at or before 2023, and the earliest start year five to ten
# years before it. We look first among the years with all parts, then among the years with
# total health spending, and fall back on 2013 to 2023.
TR <- list()
for (basis in c("parts", "che")) {
  years <- if (basis == "parts") own_parts$year else che_years
  end_years <- sort(years[years >= 2000 + MIN_SPAN & years <= MAX_YEAR], decreasing = TRUE)
  for (y1 in end_years) {
    starts <- years[years >= max(2000, y1 - WINDOW) & years <= y1 - MIN_SPAN]
    if (length(starts) > 0) {
      TR$window <- list(y0 = min(starts), y1 = y1)
      break
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(TR$window)) {
    break
  }
}
# the loop stopped on the basis that gave the window
has_parts <- !is.null(TR$window) && basis == "parts"
if (is.null(TR$window)) {
  TR$window <- list(y0 = MAX_YEAR - WINDOW, y1 = MAX_YEAR)
}
window_start <- TR$window$y0
window_end <- TR$window$y1

if (has_parts) {
  # The change of each part for every member with both years: average log points a year
  # (times 100), which add up exactly to the total
  start_parts <- filter(parts, year == window_start)
  end_parts <- filter(parts, year == window_end)
  changes <- start_parts |>
    inner_join(end_parts, by = "iso3", suffix = c("0", "1")) |>
    filter(iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS) |>
    mutate(
      span = year1 - year0,
      income = 100 * log(gdp1 / gdp0) / span,
      pie = 100 * log(pie1 / pie0) / span,
      slice = 100 * log(slice1 / slice0) / span,
      total = 100 * log(ghe1 / ghe0) / span
    )
  own_change <- filter(changes, iso3 == ISO)
  TR$dec <- c(
    income = own_change$income,
    pie = own_change$pie,
    slice = own_change$slice,
    total = own_change$total
  )
  TR$median <- c(
    income = peer_median(changes$income),
    pie = peer_median(changes$pie),
    slice = peer_median(changes$slice),
    total = peer_median(changes$total)
  )
  TR$median_n <- sum(is.finite(changes$total))

  # Spending growth in the two halves of the window, for the timing chart. The deck rounds a
  # half year up (JavaScript's Math.round), so we take the ceiling.
  mid <- window_start + ceiling((window_end - window_start) / 2)
  ghe_mid <- own_parts$ghe[own_parts$year == mid]
  if (length(ghe_mid) > 0 && mid > window_start && mid < window_end) {
    TR$halves <- list(
      mid = mid,
      first = 100 * log(ghe_mid / own_change$ghe0) / (mid - window_start),
      second = 100 * log(own_change$ghe1 / ghe_mid) / (window_end - mid)
    )
  }
}

# Total real health spending from all sources over the same window, for countries without
# the split
che_start <- own_fin$che_usd2023_pc[match(window_start, own_fin$year)]
che_end <- own_fin$che_usd2023_pc[match(window_end, own_fin$year)]
if (is.finite(che_start) && is.finite(che_end) && che_start > 0 && che_end > 0) {
  che_at_start <- fin_wide |>
    filter(year == window_start) |>
    select(iso3, c0 = che_usd2023_pc)
  che_at_end <- fin_wide |>
    filter(year == window_end) |>
    select(iso3, c1 = che_usd2023_pc)
  che_change <- che_at_start |>
    inner_join(che_at_end, by = "iso3") |>
    filter(iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS, c0 > 0, c1 > 0) |>
    mutate(rate = 100 * log(c1 / c0) / (window_end - window_start))
  TR$che <- list(
    value = 100 * log(che_end / che_start) / (window_end - window_start),
    median = peer_median(che_change$rate)
  )
}

# The outcome rows. better = +1 when higher is better; tol is the smallest change in the gap
# that counts; back is how far before the window end the latest value may be (premature NCD
# mortality ends in 2021, so three years).
ROWS <- data.frame(
  id = c("life", "u5", "maternal", "uhc", "oops_che", "ncd"),
  better = c(1, -1, -1, 1, -1, -1),
  gap = c("diff", "ratio", "ratio", "diff", "diff", "ratio"),
  tol = c(0.5, 0.05, 0.05, 2, 2, 0.05),
  back = c(2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 3)
)
trend_rows <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(ROWS))) {
  row <- ROWS[i, ]
  if (row$id == "oops_che") {
    series <- fin |>
      filter(code == row$id) |>
      transmute(iso3, year, value)
  } else {
    series <- filter(outc, id == row$id)
  }
  own_series <- filter(series, iso3 == ISO)

  # the start: the first value in the window's first three years; the latest: at the window
  # end or a little before
  in_first_years <- own_series$year >= window_start & own_series$year <= window_start + 2
  near_the_end <- own_series$year <= window_end & own_series$year >= window_end - row$back
  start_years <- own_series$year[in_first_years]
  latest_years <- own_series$year[near_the_end]
  if (length(start_years) == 0 || length(latest_years) == 0) next
  if (max(latest_years) - min(start_years) < 3) next
  start_year <- min(start_years)
  latest_year <- max(latest_years)
  start_value <- own_series$value[own_series$year == start_year]
  latest_value <- own_series$value[own_series$year == latest_year]

  # the income-group median at both ends: GHED's own statistics for out-of-pocket payments,
  # the members' values otherwise
  if (row$id == "oops_che") {
    start_median <- inc_medians$oops_che[match(start_year, inc_medians$year)]
    latest_median <- inc_medians$oops_che[match(latest_year, inc_medians$year)]
  } else {
    members_start <- filter(series, year == start_year, iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS)
    members_latest <- filter(series, year == latest_year, iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS)
    start_median <- peer_median(members_start$value)
    latest_median <- peer_median(members_latest$value)
  }

  # the gap to the median, above zero when better: a log ratio for mortality, a difference
  # otherwise
  if (row$gap == "ratio") {
    start_ok <- start_value > 0 && is.finite(start_median) && start_median > 0
    latest_ok <- latest_value > 0 && is.finite(latest_median) && latest_median > 0
    gap_start <- if (start_ok) row$better * log(start_value / start_median) else NA
    gap_latest <- if (latest_ok) row$better * log(latest_value / latest_median) else NA
  } else {
    gap_start <- row$better * (start_value - start_median)
    gap_latest <- row$better * (latest_value - latest_median)
  }
  change <- gap_latest - gap_start
  steady <- abs(change) < row$tol
  verdict <- case_when(
    !is.finite(gap_start) | !is.finite(gap_latest) ~ "na",
    steady & abs(gap_latest) < row$tol / 2 ~ "close",
    steady & gap_latest < 0 ~ "gapSteady",
    steady ~ "leadSteady",
    gap_start < 0 & gap_latest >= 0 ~ "nowAhead",
    gap_start >= 0 & gap_latest < 0 ~ "nowBehind",
    gap_start < 0 & change > 0 ~ "narrowing",
    gap_start < 0 ~ "widening",
    change > 0 ~ "leadGrowing",
    TRUE ~ "leadShrinking"
  )
  trend_rows[[row$id]] <- data.frame(
    id = row$id,
    start_year = start_year,
    start = start_value,
    latest_year = latest_year,
    latest = latest_value,
    gap_start = gap_start,
    gap_latest = gap_latest,
    verdict = verdict
  )
}

# Financial hardship comes from surveys: we compare the first and the latest survey inside the
# window, calling a move of 1 point or more improving or worsening
hardship <- outc |>
  filter(id == "hardship", iso3 == ISO, year >= window_start, year <= window_end) |>
  arrange(year)
if (nrow(hardship) > 0) {
  members_last <- outc |>
    filter(id == "hardship", iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS, year >= window_start, year <= window_end) |>
    group_by(iso3) |>
    slice_max(year, n = 1)
  first_survey <- hardship[1, ]
  latest_survey <- hardship[nrow(hardship), ]
  several <- nrow(hardship) > 1
  improvement <- -1 * (latest_survey$value - first_survey$value) # less hardship is better
  verdict <- case_when(
    !several ~ "oneSurvey",
    improvement >= 1 ~ "improving",
    improvement <= -1 ~ "worsening",
    TRUE ~ "flat"
  )
  trend_rows$hardship <- data.frame(
    id = "hardship",
    start_year = if (several) first_survey$year else NA,
    start = if (several) first_survey$value else NA,
    latest_year = latest_survey$year,
    latest = latest_survey$value,
    gap_start = NA,
    gap_latest = -1 * (latest_survey$value - peer_median(members_last$value)),
    verdict = verdict
  )
}
TR$rows <- bind_rows(trend_rows)
if (nrow(TR$rows) == 0) {
  # no outcome row at all: an empty table with the same columns, so later filters still work
  TR$rows <- data.frame(
    id = character(),
    start_year = numeric(),
    start = numeric(),
    latest_year = numeric(),
    latest = numeric(),
    gap_start = numeric(),
    gap_latest = numeric(),
    verdict = character()
  )
}
```

## Health for spending: the cross-country fit

For each health-for-spending measure, we fit a least-squares line relating the outcome (natural log for the three mortality rates) to the base-10 log of current health spending per person across all countries with both values in the same year. The fit year is the latest at or before 2023 when at least 150 countries publish spending, premature NCD mortality and two of the three mortality measures. Premature NCD mortality ends in 2021, so the fit year is 2021 for most countries. Each fit requires at least 100 countries.

We calculate a country's z score as its gap to the line divided by the fit's residual standard deviation, signed so positive is better. The health score is the mean z of premature NCD, under-five and maternal mortality, using at least two; we fit and show coverage but exclude it from the score. We score a country without data in the fit year in its latest year within five years before the fit year, against that year's own fit. We choose the four comparators as the region's countries closest in log spending, filling from the income group, and include only countries of at least a million people when the country itself has a million or more.

We fit twice, with spending at market exchange rates (annex A3) and in current PPP international dollars (slide 5), restricting the PPP fit to countries that also publish the US$ figure so both fits use the same countries.

```{r health-fit}
MEASURES <- data.frame(
  id = c("ncd", "u5", "maternal", "uhc"),
  log = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE),
  better = c(-1, -1, -1, 1),
  in_score = c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE)
)

# Health spending per person, every country and year: current US$, and current PPP where the
# US$ figure is published too, so that both fits use the same countries
spend <- fin_wide |>
  transmute(
    iso3,
    year,
    usd = ifelse(che_pc_usd > 0, che_pc_usd, NA),
    ppp = ifelse(che_pc_usd > 0 & che_ppp_pc > 0, che_ppp_pc, NA)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(c(usd, ppp), names_to = "unit", values_to = "spend") |>
  filter(!is.na(spend))

# The four measures with spending of the same year. A rate must be above zero to take its log.
health <- outc |>
  inner_join(MEASURES, by = "id") |>
  filter(!log | value > 0) |>
  inner_join(spend, by = c("iso3", "year"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(y = ifelse(log, log(value), value))

# We fit one least-squares line per spending unit, year and measure with lm(), from at least
# 100 countries: the outcome on the base-10 log of spending. sigma() is the residual standard
# deviation.
fits <- health |>
  group_by(unit, year, id) |>
  filter(n() >= 100) |>
  summarise(model = list(lm(y ~ log10(spend))), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    a = sapply(model, coef)[1, ],
    b = sapply(model, coef)[2, ],
    sd = sapply(model, sigma)
  ) |>
  select(-model)

# every country's distance from the line in residual standard deviations, positive when
# better than typical
scored <- health |>
  inner_join(fits, by = c("unit", "year", "id")) |>
  mutate(
    line = a + b * log10(spend),
    z = better * (y - line) / sd,
    expected = ifelse(log, exp(line), line),
    gap = value - expected,
    ratio = ifelse(log, value / expected, NA),
    verdict = case_when(
      !is.finite(z) ~ NA_character_,
      z >= 0.5 ~ "better",
      z <= -0.5 ~ "worse",
      TRUE ~ "close"
    )
  )

# the health score: the mean z of the three mortality measures, with at least two of them
health_score <- scored |>
  filter(in_score) |>
  select(unit, iso3, year, id, z) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = id, values_from = z) |>
  mutate(
    n_scored = (!is.na(ncd)) + (!is.na(u5)) + (!is.na(maternal)),
    z_sum = coalesce(ncd, 0) + coalesce(u5, 0) + coalesce(maternal, 0),
    z = ifelse(n_scored >= 2, z_sum / n_scored, NA)
  )

# The fit year: the latest at or before 2023 in which at least 150 countries publish
# spending, premature NCD mortality and two of the three mortality measures
fit_years <- health |>
  filter(in_score, year <= MAX_YEAR) |>
  group_by(unit, year, iso3) |>
  summarise(ok = any(id == "ncd") & n() >= 2) |>
  group_by(unit, year) |>
  summarise(countries = sum(ok)) |>
  filter(countries >= 150) |>
  group_by(unit) |>
  summarise(year = max(year))

HEALTH <- list()
for (spend_unit in c("usd", "ppp")) {
  fit_year <- fit_years$year[fit_years$unit == spend_unit]
  if (length(fit_year) == 0) {
    HEALTH[[spend_unit]] <- list(ready = FALSE, peers = data.frame())
    next
  }
  first_year <- max(2000, fit_year - 5)
  # each country's score in its latest year with one, from the fit year back five years
  scores <- health_score |>
    filter(unit == spend_unit, year <= fit_year, year >= first_year, is.finite(z)) |>
    group_by(iso3) |>
    slice_max(year, n = 1) |>
    ungroup()

  # The country: its scored year, else its latest year with any measure. The charts use that
  # year.
  own_rows <- filter(scored, unit == spend_unit, iso3 == ISO, year >= first_year, year <= fit_year)
  own_year <- NA
  if (nrow(own_rows) > 0) {
    own_year <- max(own_rows$year)
  }
  if (ISO %in% scores$iso3) {
    own_year <- scores$year[scores$iso3 == ISO]
  }
  chart_year <- if (is.na(own_year)) fit_year else own_year
  own_measures <- filter(own_rows, year == chart_year)
  country_z <- if (ISO %in% scores$iso3) scores$z[scores$iso3 == ISO] else NA_real_
  own_spend <- filter(spend, unit == spend_unit, iso3 == ISO, year == chart_year)$spend
  country <- list(
    z = country_z,
    year = own_year,
    components = own_measures,
    spend = if (is.na(own_year)) NA_real_ else own_spend,
    verdict = case_when(
      !is.finite(country_z) ~ NA_character_,
      country_z >= 0.5 ~ "better",
      country_z <= -0.5 ~ "worse",
      TRUE ~ "close"
    )
  )

  # The charted measure: premature NCD mortality, else the first measure the country has,
  # else the first measure with a line
  fits_chart_year <- filter(fits, unit == spend_unit, year == chart_year)
  main <- c(
    intersect(MEASURES$id, own_measures$id),
    intersect(MEASURES$id, fits_chart_year$id)
  )[1]
  scatter <- NULL
  peers <- data.frame()
  if (!is.na(main)) {
    others <- health |>
      filter(unit == spend_unit, year == chart_year, id == main, iso3 != ISO) |>
      select(iso3, x = spend, y = value)
    own_point <- filter(own_measures, id == main)
    scatter <- list(
      measure = main,
      year = chart_year,
      points = others,
      fit = filter(fits_chart_year, id == main),
      country = if (nrow(own_point) > 0) own_point else NULL,
      n = nrow(others) + nrow(own_point)
    )
  }
  if (!is.null(scatter$country)) {
    # The four comparators: the region's countries closest in log spending, filled from the
    # income group. When the country has a million people or more, only countries of that
    # size count (population in thousands, the year before when the chart year is missing).
    population <- fin |>
      filter(code == "pop", year %in% c(chart_year, chart_year - 1)) |>
      arrange(desc(year)) |>
      distinct(iso3, .keep_all = TRUE)
    big <- isTRUE(population$value[population$iso3 == ISO] >= 1000)
    candidates <- others |>
      left_join(select(population, iso3, pop = value), by = "iso3") |>
      filter(!big | (is.finite(pop) & pop >= 1000)) |>
      mutate(
        distance = abs(log10(x) - log10(country$spend)),
        region = iso3 %in% REG_MEMBERS
      ) |>
      arrange(distance, iso3)
    chosen <- head(filter(candidates, region), 4)
    if (nrow(chosen) < 4) {
      fill_ins <- filter(candidates, iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS, !iso3 %in% chosen$iso3)
      chosen <- bind_rows(chosen, head(fill_ins, 4 - nrow(chosen)))
    }
    z_chart_year <- filter(health_score, unit == spend_unit, year == chart_year)
    peers <- data.frame(
      iso = chosen$iso3,
      name = countries$name[match(chosen$iso3, ISOS)],
      region = chosen$region,
      spend = chosen$x,
      value = chosen$y,
      z = z_chart_year$z[match(chosen$iso3, z_chart_year$iso3)]
    )
  }
  HEALTH[[spend_unit]] <- list(
    ready = TRUE,
    year = fit_year,
    cyear = chart_year,
    scores = setNames(scores$z, scores$iso3),
    country = country,
    scatter = scatter,
    peers = peers
  )
}
HEALTH_USD <- HEALTH$usd
HEALTH_PPP <- HEALTH$ppp
```

## Financial protection for spending: the survey fit

Financial hardship is a survey measure published only every few years. We use each country's latest survey since 2000 (at or before 2023) with same-year government health spending per person. We express spending in constant 2023 dollars so surveys from different years share one scale: constant 2023 US$ for annex A4 and constant 2023 PPP dollars for slide 6 (the US$ figure times the country's 2023 ratio of PPP to US$ spending, equal to constant 2023 national-currency spending over the 2023 PPP factor).

We fit the typical hardship rate as a straight line on log spending, floored at zero. For a country without the 2025 hardship measure, we use the older measure of spending more than 10% of the household budget on health and fit it separately. The z score is the typical level minus the country's value, over the residual standard deviation; positive means less hardship than typical.

```{r protection-fit}
# Government health spending per person in constant 2023 dollars, every country and year:
# constant 2023 US$, and constant 2023 PPP dollars (the US$ figure times the country's 2023
# ratio of PPP to US$ spending)
ppp_factor <- fin_wide |>
  filter(year == BASE, che_ppp_pc > 0, che_pc_usd > 0) |>
  transmute(iso3, factor = che_ppp_pc / che_pc_usd)
gov <- fin_wide |>
  left_join(ppp_factor, by = "iso3") |>
  transmute(
    iso3,
    year,
    usd = ifelse(che_usd2023_pc > 0 & gghed_che > 0, che_usd2023_pc * gghed_che / 100, NA),
    ppp = ifelse(
      che_usd2023_pc * factor > 0 & gghed_che > 0,
      che_usd2023_pc * factor * gghed_che / 100,
      NA
    )
  )

# the surveys since 2000, at or before 2023: financial hardship (2025 definition), and the
# older measure of spending more than 10% of the household budget
hardship_surveys <- outc |>
  filter(id == "hardship") |>
  select(iso3, measure = id, year, value)
older_surveys <- fin |>
  filter(code == "cat10_oop") |>
  select(iso3, measure = code, year, value)
surveys <- bind_rows(hardship_surveys, older_surveys) |>
  filter(year >= 2000, year <= MAX_YEAR)
# the latest published share of out-of-pocket payments, for the slide's second sentence
oop_latest <- fin |>
  filter(iso3 == ISO, code == "oops_che", year <= MAX_YEAR) |>
  slice_max(year, n = 1)

PROT <- list()
for (spend_unit in c("usd", "ppp")) {
  # The survey each country enters with: its latest with government spending published for
  # the same year, else its latest survey, unpaired
  obs <- surveys |>
    left_join(select(gov, iso3, year, x = all_of(spend_unit)), by = c("iso3", "year")) |>
    mutate(paired = is.finite(x)) |>
    arrange(measure, iso3, desc(paired), desc(year)) |>
    distinct(measure, iso3, .keep_all = TRUE)

  # The typical level: a least-squares line of the rate on the log of spending, from at least
  # 8 surveys, floored at zero
  fit_lines <- obs |>
    filter(paired, is.finite(value)) |>
    group_by(measure) |>
    filter(n() >= 8) |>
    summarise(model = list(lm(value ~ log10(x))), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(
      a = sapply(model, coef)[1, ],
      b = sapply(model, coef)[2, ],
      sd = sapply(model, sigma)
    ) |>
    select(-model)
  obs <- obs |>
    left_join(fit_lines, by = "measure") |>
    mutate(
      expected = ifelse(paired, pmax(0, a + b * log10(x)), NA),
      z = ifelse(sd > 0, (expected - value) / sd, NA) # positive: less hardship than typical
    )

  # each country's score: the 2025 measure when it can be scored, else the older one
  scores <- obs |>
    filter(is.finite(z)) |>
    arrange(measure != "hardship") |>
    distinct(iso3, .keep_all = TRUE)

  # the country: the first measure with a paired survey and a line, else the first with a survey
  own_obs <- obs |>
    filter(iso3 == ISO) |>
    arrange(measure != "hardship")
  with_line <- filter(own_obs, paired, !is.na(a))
  own <- if (nrow(with_line) > 0) with_line[1, ] else own_obs[1, ]
  chosen <- if (is.na(own$measure)) "hardship" else own$measure
  own_paired <- isTRUE(own$paired)
  z <- if (own_paired) own$z else NA_real_
  country <- list(
    z = z,
    measure = own$measure,
    year = own$year,
    value = own$value,
    expected = if (own_paired) own$expected else NA_real_,
    spending = if (own_paired) own$x else NA_real_,
    verdict = case_when(
      !is.finite(z) ~ NA_character_,
      z >= 0.5 ~ "stronger",
      z <= -0.5 ~ "weaker",
      TRUE ~ "close"
    )
  )

  # The chart shows every paired survey of that measure. The income group's median takes each
  # member's survey, whatever its year.
  chart_points <- filter(obs, measure == chosen, paired)
  members <- filter(obs, measure == chosen, iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS)
  oop <- NULL
  if (nrow(oop_latest) > 0) {
    oop <- list(
      value = oop_latest$value,
      year = oop_latest$year,
      median = inc_medians$oops_che[match(oop_latest$year, inc_medians$year)]
    )
  }
  PROT[[spend_unit]] <- list(
    ready = !is.na(own$measure),
    scores = setNames(scores$z, scores$iso3),
    country = country,
    fit = if (chosen %in% fit_lines$measure) filter(fit_lines, measure == chosen) else NULL,
    points = transmute(filter(chart_points, iso3 != ISO), iso = iso3, x, y = value, year),
    years = if (nrow(chart_points) > 0) range(chart_points$year) else NULL,
    group = list(
      N = length(INC_MEMBERS),
      median = peer_median(members$value),
      n = sum(is.finite(members$value)),
      years = if (nrow(members) > 0) range(members$year) else NULL
    ),
    oop = oop
  )
}
PROT_USD <- PROT$usd
PROT_PPP <- PROT$ppp
```

## The two scores together

We call a dimension a gap when its score is 0.5 or more below zero, the rule both slides use for a result worse or weaker than typical. For the selected country, we read the two fits' verdicts as they stand.

```{r performance-gap}
GAP <- list()
GAP_KINDS <- c("neither", "health", "protection", "both")
for (spend_unit in c("usd", "ppp")) {
  health_fit <- HEALTH[[spend_unit]]
  protection_fit <- PROT[[spend_unit]]
  health_z <- if (isTRUE(is.finite(health_fit$country$z))) health_fit$country$z else NA_real_
  protection_z <- if (is.finite(protection_fit$country$z)) protection_fit$country$z else NA_real_

  # The country's gap: a score 0.5 or more below zero is a gap, and when one score is missing
  # the other decides
  health_gap <- if (is.finite(health_z)) health_z <= -0.5 else NA
  protection_gap <- if (is.finite(protection_z)) protection_z <= -0.5 else NA
  gap <- case_when(
    isTRUE(health_gap) & isTRUE(protection_gap) ~ "both",
    isTRUE(health_gap) ~ "health",
    isTRUE(protection_gap) ~ "protection",
    isFALSE(health_gap) & isFALSE(protection_gap) ~ "neither",
    TRUE ~ "unknown"
  )

  # every country with both scores, and where its gap lies
  both <- data.frame(iso = ISOS, h = NA_real_, p = NA_real_)
  if (health_fit$ready) {
    both$h <- unname(health_fit$scores[ISOS])
  }
  both$p <- unname(protection_fit$scores[ISOS])
  both$h[both$iso == ISO] <- health_z
  both$p[both$iso == ISO] <- protection_z
  both <- both |>
    filter(is.finite(h), is.finite(p)) |>
    mutate(gap = case_when(
      h <= -0.5 & p <= -0.5 ~ "both",
      h <= -0.5 ~ "health",
      p <= -0.5 ~ "protection",
      TRUE ~ "neither"
    ))
  in_group <- both$iso %in% INC_MEMBERS
  all_counts <- table(factor(both$gap, levels = GAP_KINDS))
  group_counts <- table(factor(both$gap[in_group], levels = GAP_KINDS))
  GAP[[spend_unit]] <- list(
    gap = gap,
    health = list(z = health_z, year = health_fit$country$year),
    protection = list(z = protection_z, year = protection_fit$country$year),
    points = filter(both, iso != ISO),
    counts = c(n = nrow(both), all_counts),
    group_counts = c(n = sum(in_group), group_counts),
    peers = if (nrow(health_fit$peers) > 0) health_fit$peers else data.frame()
  )
}
GAP_USD <- GAP$usd
GAP_PPP <- GAP$ppp
```

## Budgets, services and the health workforce

We compare government health spending per person with the income-group median in the latest year when both exist, in current US$ (annex A5) and current PPP international dollars (slide 8). For service coverage and workforce, we use each country's latest value in the ten years to 2023; the median uses members' latest values in that window. Values more than 10% below the median are shortfalls.

On the workforce slide, we add doctors to nurses and midwives only in a year when both are reported. Each year's median uses members' latest combined value in the five years to that year; a same-year median would fail the reporting rule in most years.

```{r services-workforce}
SVC_IDS <- c("uhc", "measles", "births", "tb_success", "art")
svc_start <- MAX_YEAR - 10 + 1 # the ten years to 2023

# Government health spending per person against its median, in US$ and in PPP: the latest
# year with a publishable median, else the latest year without one
spend_rows <- list()
for (spend_unit in c("usd", "ppp")) {
  series <- if (spend_unit == "usd") "gghed_pc_usd" else "gghed_ppp_pc"
  medians <- inc_stats |>
    filter(code == series, !suppressed, is.finite(median)) |>
    select(year, median)
  own_spending <- fin |>
    filter(iso3 == ISO, code == series, year <= MAX_YEAR) |>
    left_join(medians, by = "year") |>
    arrange(desc(year))
  with_median <- filter(own_spending, is.finite(median))
  pick <- if (nrow(with_median) > 0) with_median[1, ] else own_spending[1, ]
  spend_rows[[spend_unit]] <- data.frame(
    id = "spending",
    value = pick$value,
    year = pick$year,
    median = pick$median
  )
}

# Service coverage: each country's latest value in the window, and the median of the members'
# latest values
latest_svc <- outc |>
  filter(id %in% SVC_IDS, year >= svc_start, year <= MAX_YEAR) |>
  group_by(iso3, id) |>
  slice_max(year, n = 1) |>
  ungroup()
own_services <- latest_svc |>
  filter(iso3 == ISO) |>
  select(id, value, year)
service_medians <- latest_svc |>
  filter(iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(median = peer_median(value))
services <- tibble(id = SVC_IDS) |>
  left_join(own_services, by = "id") |>
  left_join(service_medians, by = "id")

# One table per spending unit: spending first, then the five services, each as a ratio to its
# median; a ratio more than 10% below the median is a shortfall
SVC <- list(window = c(svc_start, MAX_YEAR), N = length(INC_MEMBERS))
for (spend_unit in c("usd", "ppp")) {
  SVC[[spend_unit]] <- bind_rows(spend_rows[[spend_unit]], services) |>
    mutate(
      ratio = ifelse(is.finite(value) & is.finite(median) & median > 0, value / median, NA),
      shortfall = is.finite(ratio) & ratio < 0.9
    )
}

# Doctors, nurses and beds count here only for whether the chain can be drawn at all
latest_inputs <- workforce |>
  filter(year >= svc_start, year <= MAX_YEAR) |>
  group_by(iso3, code) |>
  slice_max(year, n = 1) |>
  ungroup()
input_medians <- latest_inputs |>
  filter(iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS) |>
  group_by(code) |>
  summarise(median = peer_median(value))
input_ratios <- latest_inputs |>
  filter(iso3 == ISO, code %in% c("SH.MED.PHYS.ZS", "SH.MED.NUMW.P3", "SH.MED.BEDS.ZS")) |>
  left_join(input_medians, by = "code") |>
  mutate(ratio = ifelse(is.finite(median) & median > 0, value / median, NA))
SVC$ready <- any(is.finite(c(SVC$usd$ratio, input_ratios$ratio)))

# The workforce: doctors plus nurses and midwives per 1,000, in years where both are reported
WF_THRESHOLD <- 4.45
wf_first <- max(2000, MAX_YEAR - 18)
wf <- workforce |>
  filter(code %in% c("SH.MED.PHYS.ZS", "SH.MED.NUMW.P3")) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = code, values_from = value) |>
  rename(phys = SH.MED.PHYS.ZS, nurse = SH.MED.NUMW.P3) |>
  mutate(both = phys + nurse)
wf_own <- wf |>
  filter(iso3 == ISO, is.finite(both), year >= wf_first, year <= MAX_YEAR) |>
  arrange(year)

# The median of each year is the median of the members' latest combined value in the five
# years to that year; a same-year median would fail the reporting rule in most years
wf_medians <- data.frame(year = wf_first:MAX_YEAR, value = NA_real_)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(wf_medians))) {
  median_year <- wf_medians$year[i]
  members_latest <- wf |>
    filter(iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS, is.finite(both)) |>
    filter(year >= median_year - 5 + 1, year <= median_year) |>
    group_by(iso3) |>
    slice_max(year, n = 1)
  wf_medians$value[i] <- peer_median(members_latest$both)
}
WF <- list(
  ready = nrow(wf_own) > 0,
  pts = wf_own,
  medians = wf_medians,
  N = length(INC_MEMBERS)
)
if (WF$ready) {
  last <- wf_own[nrow(wf_own), ]
  # the earlier point: the first year three to ten years before the latest
  earlier <- filter(wf_own, year >= last$year - 10, year <= last$year - 3)
  WF$latest <- list(
    year = last$year,
    value = last$both,
    phys = last$phys,
    nurse = last$nurse,
    median = wf_medians$value[wf_medians$year == last$year]
  )
  if (nrow(earlier) > 0) {
    WF$earlier <- list(
      year = earlier$year[1],
      value = earlier$both[1],
      median = wf_medians$value[wf_medians$year == earlier$year[1]]
    )
  }
}
# doctors and nurses on their own, for the sentence when they are never reported for the
# same year
own_wf <- workforce |>
  filter(iso3 == ISO, year >= 1990, year <= MAX_YEAR) |>
  arrange(year)
phys_last <- tail(filter(own_wf, code == "SH.MED.PHYS.ZS"), 1)
nurse_last <- tail(filter(own_wf, code == "SH.MED.NUMW.P3"), 1)
```

## Medicines, prevention and need

The medicine measure covers purchases outside a visit or stay (WHO health accounts, line HC.5.1) over the ten years to 2023; the median uses members' latest values. For the prevention-to-treatment comparison, we use the first available source in this order: WHO health accounts for government spending (preventive care HC.6 against curative care HC.1), IMF general government spending by function (public health against hospital and outpatient services), then WHO health accounts from all sources. We exclude the IMF series if its public health share ever exceeds 35%, changes by more than 20 points in one year, or leaves half of the latest year unclassified. Such series reflect spending classifications rather than what the spending buys.

We read need from eleven burden and coverage measures, each divided by the income-group median of the same year (for survey measures, the latest value in ten years). We turn coverage into the share not reached, counting gaps under 5 points as 5 so that a near-universal service does not produce a large ratio from a tiny difference.

```{r medicines-prevention-need}
recent <- MAX_YEAR - 10 + 1 # the ten years to 2023

# Medicines bought outside a visit or a stay: the country's bars, and the median of the
# members' latest shares
med <- medicines |>
  filter(year >= recent, year <= MAX_YEAR, is.finite(share)) |>
  arrange(year)
med_bars <- filter(med, iso3 == ISO)
med_members <- med |>
  filter(iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS) |>
  group_by(iso3) |>
  slice_max(year, n = 1)
med_split <- filter(med_bars, is.finite(pvt)) # the years in which the accounts say who paid
avail <- med_avail |>
  filter(iso3 == ISO, year <= MAX_YEAR, is.finite(value)) |>
  slice_max(year, n = 1)
MED <- list(
  ready = nrow(med_bars) > 0,
  window = c(recent, MAX_YEAR),
  bars = med_bars,
  last = if (nrow(med_bars) > 0) med_bars[nrow(med_bars), ] else NULL,
  last_split = if (nrow(med_split) > 0) med_split[nrow(med_split), ] else NULL,
  median = peer_median(med_members$share),
  n = sum(is.finite(med_members$share)),
  avail = if (nrow(avail) > 0) avail else NULL
)

# Prevention against treatment, from the first source that has it
own_prevention <- prevention |>
  filter(iso3 == ISO, year <= MAX_YEAR) |>
  arrange(year)
prev_gov <- own_prevention |>
  filter(is.finite(gov_prev)) |>
  select(year, prev = gov_prev, cur = gov_cur)
prev_all <- own_prevention |>
  filter(is.finite(all_prev)) |>
  select(year, prev = all_prev, cur = all_cur)
# IMF spending by function: public health (GF0740) against hospital (GF073) and outpatient
# (GF072) services, with the unclassified line (GF0760)
prev_cofog <- cofog |>
  filter(iso3 == ISO, year >= MAX_YEAR - 18, year <= MAX_YEAR) |>
  mutate(line = factor(line, levels = c("GF0740_T", "GF073_T", "GF072_T", "GF0760_T"))) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = line, values_from = share_of_health, names_expand = TRUE) |>
  filter(!is.na(GF0740_T)) |>
  arrange(year) |>
  transmute(year, prev = GF0740_T, cur = GF073_T + GF072_T, uncl = GF0760_T)

# We drop the IMF series when it reflects classification rather than spending: a public
# health share above 35%, a move of more than 20 points in one year, or half of the latest
# year unclassified
largest_move <- if (nrow(prev_cofog) > 1) max(0, abs(diff(prev_cofog$prev))) else 0
last_unclassified <- if (nrow(prev_cofog) > 0) prev_cofog$uncl[nrow(prev_cofog)] else NA
cofog_ok <- nrow(prev_cofog) >= 3 &&
  any(prev_cofog$prev > 0) &&
  !(is.finite(last_unclassified) && last_unclassified >= 50) &&
  max(prev_cofog$prev) <= 35 &&
  largest_move <= 20
if (!cofog_ok) {
  prev_cofog <- prev_cofog[0, ]
}

# the source: government accounts with two years or more, then the IMF, then all sources,
# then any single year
tier <- case_when(
  nrow(prev_gov) >= 2 ~ "gov",
  nrow(prev_cofog) > 0 ~ "cofog",
  nrow(prev_all) >= 2 ~ "all",
  nrow(prev_gov) > 0 ~ "gov",
  nrow(prev_all) > 0 ~ "all",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)
pts <- NULL
if (identical(tier, "gov")) pts <- prev_gov
if (identical(tier, "cofog")) pts <- select(prev_cofog, year, prev, cur)
if (identical(tier, "all")) pts <- prev_all
PREV <- list(ready = !is.na(tier), tier = tier, pts = pts, window = c(recent, MAX_YEAR))
if (identical(tier, "gov")) {
  # the median of the members' latest government preventive share in the ten years
  latest_prev <- prevention |>
    filter(iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS, year >= recent, year <= MAX_YEAR, is.finite(gov_prev)) |>
    group_by(iso3) |>
    slice_max(year, n = 1)
  PREV$median <- list(value = peer_median(latest_prev$gov_prev), n = nrow(latest_prev))
}
if (PREV$ready) {
  # We flag the longest run of three or more consecutive years with the same preventive share,
  # since one year's split was then probably applied to the others
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(pts))) {
    j <- i
    while (j < nrow(pts)) {
      next_is_consecutive <- pts$year[j + 1] == pts$year[j] + 1
      next_is_same <- abs(pts$prev[j + 1] - pts$prev[i]) < 0.05
      if (!(next_is_consecutive && next_is_same)) break
      j <- j + 1
    }
    run_length <- j - i
    longest_so_far <- if (is.null(PREV$flat)) -Inf else PREV$flat[2] - PREV$flat[1]
    if (run_length >= 2 && run_length > longest_so_far) {
      PREV$flat <- c(pts$year[i], pts$year[j])
    }
  }
  # and the one-year moves over 10 points outside 2020 to 2022
  move_end_years <- pts$year[-1]
  move_start_years <- pts$year[-nrow(pts)]
  large_moves <- abs(diff(pts$prev)) > 10 &
    !(move_end_years %in% 2020:2022) &
    !(move_start_years %in% 2020:2022)
  PREV$swings <- move_end_years[large_moves]
}

# Need: eleven burden and coverage measures against the income-group median, with coverage
# turned into the share not reached
NEED_SPECS <- data.frame(
  id = c(
    "u5", "maternal", "stunting", "tb", "hiv", "malaria", "ncd", "dtp", "births", "art",
    "tb_success"
  ),
  kind = c(rep("burden", 7), rep("gap", 4)),
  survey = c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, FALSE),
  short = c(
    "under-five mortality",
    "maternal mortality",
    "child stunting",
    "tuberculosis incidence",
    "HIV incidence",
    "malaria incidence",
    "premature NCD mortality",
    "the share of children without DTP3",
    "the share of births without a skilled attendant",
    "the share of people with HIV not on treatment",
    "the share of TB cases not treated successfully"
  )
)
need_data <- outc |>
  filter(id %in% NEED_SPECS$id, year >= recent, year <= MAX_YEAR) |>
  left_join(NEED_SPECS, by = "id") |>
  mutate(need = ifelse(kind == "gap", pmax(0, 100 - value), value))
need_rows <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(NEED_SPECS))) {
  spec <- NEED_SPECS[i, ]
  own_need <- need_data |>
    filter(iso3 == ISO, id == spec$id) |>
    arrange(desc(year))
  if (nrow(own_need) == 0) next
  need_year <- NA
  if (spec$survey) {
    # a survey measure: the median of the members' latest values in the ten years
    members <- need_data |>
      filter(id == spec$id, iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS) |>
      group_by(iso3) |>
      slice_max(year, n = 1)
    need_median <- peer_median(members$need)
    if (is.finite(need_median)) {
      need_year <- own_need$year[1]
    }
  } else {
    # an annual measure: the latest year, or up to five years back, with a publishable median
    # of the same year
    for (y in own_need$year[own_need$year >= own_need$year[1] - 5]) {
      members <- filter(need_data, id == spec$id, year == y, iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS)
      need_median <- peer_median(members$need)
      if (is.finite(need_median)) {
        need_year <- y
        break
      }
    }
  }
  if (is.na(need_year)) next
  value <- own_need$need[own_need$year == need_year]
  # A gap under 5 points counts as 5, so that a near-universal service does not give a large
  # ratio from a tiny difference
  if (spec$kind == "gap") {
    ratio <- max(value, 5) / max(need_median, 5)
  } else if (need_median > 0) {
    ratio <- value / need_median
  } else {
    next
  }
  need_rows[[spec$id]] <- data.frame(
    id = spec$id,
    kind = spec$kind,
    short = spec$short,
    year = need_year,
    value = value,
    median = need_median,
    ratio = ratio
  )
}
NEED <- bind_rows(need_rows)
if (nrow(NEED) > 0) {
  # burden first, then gaps, each by ratio
  NEED <- arrange(NEED, kind != "burden", desc(ratio))
}
```

## Pooling and provider payment

We split current health spending by financing scheme in the latest year with country compulsory and out-of-pocket shares and publishable medians for both. Government schemes are compulsory schemes less compulsory insurance; voluntary schemes exclude out-of-pocket payments. For these differences, we take the median of members' differences under the same reporting rule. We read a small negative value from rounding (above -0.05) as zero.

We use the country's payment record to show how providers are paid. Where the record names neither a purchaser nor a payment arrangement, we take both from a compilation of public sources. We omit state-to-insurer payments, which are pooling flows, and methods no longer in use. The slide reports only the care level and main payment method.

```{r pooling-payment}
# The financing schemes, every country and year, as % of current health spending: compulsory
# schemes, of which government schemes (compulsory less compulsory insurance) and compulsory
# insurance; voluntary schemes (less out-of-pocket payments, which GHED counts with them); and
# out-of-pocket payments. We read a rounding residue above -0.05 as zero.
schemes <- fin_wide |>
  transmute(
    iso3,
    year,
    cfa = cfa_che,
    gov = cfa_che - chi_che,
    chi = chi_che,
    vol = vfa_che - oops_che,
    oop = oops_che
  ) |>
  mutate(across(
    c(cfa, gov, chi, vol, oop),
    ~ ifelse(is.finite(.x) & .x < 0 & .x > -0.05, 0, .x)
  ))
own_schemes <- schemes |>
  filter(iso3 == ISO, year <= MAX_YEAR, is.finite(cfa), is.finite(oop)) |>
  arrange(desc(year))

# The year: the latest with the country's compulsory and out-of-pocket shares and
# publishable medians for both
ok_years <- inc_stats |>
  filter(code %in% c("cfa_che", "oops_che"), !suppressed, is.finite(median)) |>
  count(year) |>
  filter(n == 2)
POOL <- list(ready = nrow(own_schemes) > 0)
if (POOL$ready) {
  comparable <- own_schemes$year[own_schemes$year %in% ok_years$year]
  POOL$peer_ok <- length(comparable) > 0
  POOL$year <- if (POOL$peer_ok) comparable[1] else own_schemes$year[1]
  own <- filter(own_schemes, year == POOL$year)
  members <- filter(schemes, year == POOL$year, iso3 %in% INC_MEMBERS)
  rows <- data.frame(
    id = c("cfa", "gov", "chi", "vol", "oop"),
    value = c(own$cfa, own$gov, own$chi, own$vol, own$oop),
    median = NA_real_,
    q1 = NA_real_,
    q3 = NA_real_
  )
  if (POOL$peer_ok) {
    # GHED's published statistics for the three published series; for the two differences,
    # the members' own differences under the same reporting rule. The quartiles interpolate
    # between ranks, R's type 7, as the deck computes them.
    published <- filter(inc_stats, year == POOL$year, !suppressed, is.finite(median))
    published_series <- c(cfa = "cfa_che", chi = "chi_che", oop = "oops_che")
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(rows))) {
      series <- published_series[rows$id[i]] # NA for the two differences
      if (!is.na(series)) {
        stat <- filter(published, code == series)
        if (nrow(stat) > 0) {
          rows[i, c("median", "q1", "q3")] <- stat[, c("median", "q1", "q3")]
        }
      } else {
        member_values <- members[[rows$id[i]]]
        group_median <- peer_median(member_values)
        if (is.finite(group_median)) {
          quartiles <- quantile(
            member_values, c(0.25, 0.75),
            na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE, type = 7
          )
          rows[i, c("median", "q1", "q3")] <- c(group_median, quartiles)
        }
      }
    }
  }
  # rest-of-world schemes or unclassified, shown from 0.1 points
  pool_row <- filter(own_fin, year == POOL$year)
  rest <- 100 - pool_row$cfa_che - pool_row$vfa_che
  if (is.finite(rest) && rest >= 0.1) {
    rows <- bind_rows(rows, data.frame(id = "rest", value = rest))
  }
  POOL$rows <- rows
  ext_median <- inc_medians$ext_che[match(POOL$year, inc_medians$year)]
  POOL$ext <- list(
    value = pool_row$ext_che,
    median = if (POOL$peer_ok) ext_median else NA_real_
  )
}

# The provider payment record. We take the arrangements as recorded, else those of the
# compilation of public sources when the record names neither a purchaser nor an arrangement.
# Payments to an insurer (pooling flows) and former methods are left out.
rec <- filter(pay_rec, iso3 == ISO)
PAY <- list(present = nrow(rec) == 1 && isTRUE(rec$has_record))
if (PAY$present) {
  arr <- filter(pay_arr, iso3 == ISO, source == "record")
  record_is_empty <- rec$record_arrangements == 0 && rec$record_purchasers == 0
  compilation_has_some <- isTRUE(
    rec$compilation_arrangements > 0 | rec$compilation_purchasers > 0
  )
  if (record_is_empty && compilation_has_some) {
    insurer_pattern <- "^(health )?insur|insurance administrator|payment to purchasers"
    arr <- pay_arr |>
      filter(iso3 == ISO, source == "compilation") |>
      filter(!(recipient_level %in% "purchaser")) |>
      filter(!grepl(insurer_pattern, coalesce(provider_label, ""), ignore.case = TRUE)) |>
      filter(!(implementation_status %in% "former"))
    PAY$supplement <- list(n_sources = rec$compilation_sources)
  }
  supplement_sources <- if (is.null(PAY$supplement)) 0 else rec$compilation_sources
  PAY$n_sources <- rec$record_sources + supplement_sources

  # care levels as the deck groups, orders and names them
  CARE <- tribble(
    ~level,                      ~care,           ~rank, ~title,
    "primary",                   "primary",       0,     "Primary care",
    "ambulatory",                "ambulatory",    1,     "Outpatient care",
    "specialist",                "specialist",    2,     "Specialist outpatient care",
    "inpatient_and_specialist",  "hospital",      3,     "Hospital care",
    "inpatient",                 "hospital",      3,     "Hospital care",
    "inpatient_and_day_care",    "hospital",      3,     "Hospital care",
    "secondary_and_tertiary",    "hospital",      3,     "Hospital care",
    "multiple_levels",           "multi",         4,     "Several levels",
    "all_covered_part_c_levels", "multi",         4,     "Several levels",
    "retail",                    "retail",        5,     "Pharmacies",
    "hospital_inpatient",        "hospital",      3,     "Hospital inpatient care",
    "hospital_outpatient",       "hospital_out",  3,     "Hospital outpatient care",
    "pharmacy",                  "retail",        5,     "Pharmacies",
    "public_health",             "public_health", 5,     "Public health programmes",
    "other",                     "other",         6,     "Other"
  )
  method_names <- rename(pay_methods, method_label = label)
  PAY$groups <- arr |>
    left_join(CARE, by = c(care_level = "level")) |>
    left_join(method_names, by = c(payment_method_id = "id")) |>
    mutate(
      care = coalesce(care, care_level, "other"),
      rank = coalesce(rank, 6),
      title = coalesce(title, gsub("_", " ", care_level)),
      main = role %in% c("base", "alternative_base"),
      method = coalesce(payment_method, method_label, payment_method_id),
      # we write dashes out: an unspaced dash reads "to" ("2-3" becomes "2 to 3"), a spaced
      # one becomes a comma
      method = gsub("(\\S)[\u2013\u2014](\\S)", "\\1 to \\2", method, perl = TRUE),
      method = gsub("\\s*[\u2013\u2014]\\s*", ", ", method),
      method = trimws(gsub("\\s+", " ", method))
    ) |>
    distinct(care, payment_method_id, main, role = ifelse(main, "main", role), .keep_all = TRUE)

  # a key tension of a fixed population payment beside payment per classified case
  tension <- sub(
    "^.*?potential tension:\\s*", "", rec$key_tension,
    ignore.case = TRUE, perl = TRUE
  )
  names_a_tension <- isTRUE(grepl("potential tension", rec$key_tension, ignore.case = TRUE))
  PAY$cap_case <- names_a_tension &&
    grepl("fixed population payment", tension, ignore.case = TRUE) &&
    grepl("per classified case", tension, ignore.case = TRUE)
  record_texts <- c(
    rec$pooling_dimension,
    rec$narrative_purchasing,
    rec$narrative_payment,
    rec$narrative_architecture
  )
  record_texts <- record_texts[!is.na(record_texts)]
  PAY$fragmentation <- any(grepl("fragment", record_texts, ignore.case = TRUE))
}
```

## Fiscal space and funding

We start the projection from the base-year spending identity. We use the IMF World Economic Outlook of October 2026 for real GDP per person and general government spending (% of GDP), as ratios to base-year values. Without an IMF path, we use the country's past growth; without past growth, we hold the economy constant. The passive scenario holds health's share of government spending; the illustrative scenario raises the share one point a year from 2027, the year after the IMF vintage, up to the share exceeded by a quarter of all countries (the world's upper quartile, base year). We use horizons of 1, 3 and 5 years after 2026. We split the change from the base year exactly in a fixed order: growth, then the budget, then the health share.

On the funding slide, we value each scenario at the last horizon. Extra spending is the change in government health spending per person times population, carried forward with UN projections. We estimate deaths averted by applying a spending elasticity of mortality of -0.13, from a meta-regression of 65 studies (Gallet and Doucouliagos 2017), to projected deaths, holding other sources of health spending at their latest level. We value those lives using full income: a statistical life at 160 times income per person before age 75, less at older ages (Lancet Commission on Investing in Health, 2024). Both are illustrative cross-country associations, not forecasts.

```{r projection-funding}
VINTAGE <- 2026 # the IMF World Economic Outlook of October 2026
HORIZONS <- c(1, 3, 5) # years after the start
STEP <- 1 # the illustrative rise of health's share, points a year
PROJ <- list(ready = ID$ready && is.finite(ID$ghe_pc))
if (PROJ$ready) {
  base_year <- ID$year # the base year of the identity
  base_ghe <- ID$ghe_pc
  base_share <- ID$gghed_gge
  pop_thousands <- own_fin$pop[match(base_year, own_fin$year)]
  PROJ$base <- list(
    year = base_year,
    ghe_pc = base_ghe,
    pop = if (is.finite(pop_thousands)) round(pop_thousands * 1000) else NA_real_
  )
  # the horizons count from 2026; a base year before 2019 counts them from itself
  projection_start <- if (base_year >= 2019) VINTAGE else base_year
  PROJ$start <- projection_start
  years <- c(if (projection_start > base_year) projection_start, projection_start + HORIZONS)

  # Growth and the budget as ratios to the base year. We use the IMF path when it covers every
  # year with positive values, else past growth (slide 4's economy part), else no growth; the
  # budget's share of GDP is otherwise held.
  weo <- filter(imf_weo, iso3 == ISO)
  gdp_path <- weo$gdp_pc_real[match(c(base_year, years), weo$year)]
  spend_path <- weo$expenditure[match(c(base_year, years), weo$year)]
  past_growth <- if (is.null(TR$dec)) NA_real_ else TR$dec[["income"]]
  if (all(is.finite(gdp_path) & gdp_path > 0)) {
    growth_ratio <- gdp_path[-1] / gdp_path[1]
    last_ratio <- growth_ratio[length(growth_ratio)]
    yearly_rate <- log(last_ratio) / (projection_start + 5 - base_year) * 100
    PROJ$growth <- list(source = "weo", rate = yearly_rate)
  } else if (is.finite(past_growth)) {
    growth_ratio <- exp(past_growth / 100 * (years - base_year))
    PROJ$growth <- list(
      source = "past",
      rate = past_growth,
      y0 = TR$window$y0,
      y1 = TR$window$y1
    )
  } else {
    growth_ratio <- rep(1, length(years))
    PROJ$growth <- list(source = "none", rate = NA_real_)
  }
  # the budget's share of GDP, as a ratio to the base year
  if (all(is.finite(spend_path) & spend_path > 0)) {
    budget_ratio <- spend_path[-1] / spend_path[1]
    PROJ$budget <- "weo"
  } else {
    budget_ratio <- rep(1, length(years))
    PROJ$budget <- "held"
  }
  PROJ$imf_actual <- if (nrow(weo) > 0) weo$last_actual[1] else NA_real_

  # Health's share is held to the start year, then rises one point a year, never above the
  # share that a quarter of all countries exceed (the world's upper quartile in the base year).
  # It is held when it is already there.
  world <- gstats |>
    filter(grouping == "global", key == "world", code == "gghed_gge", year == base_year)
  world_ok <- nrow(world) > 0 && !world$suppressed && is.finite(world$q3)
  share_cap <- if (world_ok) world$q3 else NA_real_
  capped <- is.finite(share_cap) && base_share >= share_cap
  share <- base_share + STEP * (years - projection_start)
  if (is.finite(share_cap)) {
    share <- pmin(share, share_cap)
  }
  share[years <= projection_start | capped] <- base_share
  PROJ$share <- list(
    base = base_share,
    ceiling = share_cap,
    capped = capped,
    at = setNames(share, years)
  )

  # the change from the base year, split in a fixed order: growth, then the budget, then the
  # health share
  trend <- base_ghe * growth_ratio * budget_ratio
  priority <- trend * (share / base_share)
  PROJ$rows <- data.frame(
    year = years,
    h = years - projection_start,
    trend = trend,
    priority = priority,
    share = share,
    growth = base_ghe * (growth_ratio - 1),
    budget = base_ghe * growth_ratio * (budget_ratio - 1),
    prio = priority - trend
  )
  share_stats <- filter(inc_stats, code == "gghed_gge", year == base_year, !suppressed)
  PROJ$comp <- list(
    share_median = if (nrow(share_stats) > 0) share_stats$median else NA_real_,
    share_q3 = if (nrow(share_stats) > 0) share_stats$q3 else NA_real_
  )
}

FUND <- list(ready = PROJ$ready)
if (FUND$ready) {
  base_year <- PROJ$base$year
  base_ghe <- PROJ$base$ghe_pc
  FUND$base <- list(year = base_year, ghe = base_ghe)
  un_country <- filter(wpp, iso3 == ISO)

  # The population in persons, carried forward with the UN projection. GHED's figure is in
  # thousands; we apply the factor of 1,000 when that brings it closer to the UN figure.
  un_pop_base <- un_country$population[match(base_year, un_country$year)]
  site_pop <- own_fin$pop[match(base_year, own_fin$year)]
  base_pop <- case_when(
    is.finite(PROJ$base$pop) & PROJ$base$pop > 0 ~ PROJ$base$pop,
    is.finite(site_pop) ~ site_pop * 1000,
    TRUE ~ un_pop_base
  )
  factor_fits <- is.finite(base_pop) && is.finite(un_pop_base) && un_pop_base > 0 &&
    abs(log(base_pop * 1000 / un_pop_base)) < abs(log(base_pop / un_pop_base))
  if (factor_fits) {
```
